# awgym

> An ARC training gym — a game a world model can watch, and six roles that play through it.

A world model is only as good as the play it watches. Solver runs stream past, checkpoints get trained on whatever happened to be recorded, and nobody can answer "did the model actually get better at predicting the next grid?" against transitions it has never seen.

## Install

```
pip install awgym
```

## Use it in 30 seconds

Play one ARC game end-to-end with the world model watching every transition, then ask it to predict the next grid and watch the surprise score fall.

## Composes with

- [awdk](https://aitherium.github.io/awdk/) — Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.
- [awm](https://aitherium.github.io/awm/) — A portable, scoped agent memory.
- [awrelay](https://aitherium.github.io/awrelay/) — Portable agent messaging — findings, alerts, coordination.
- [awgit](https://aitherium.github.io/awgit/) — Semantic version control on top of git — edit-ops and leases.
- [awgraph](https://aitherium.github.io/awgraph/) — A semantic code graph for agents — AST + tree-sitter, call graphs.
- [awfocus](https://aitherium.github.io/awfocus/) — See, search and steer every Claude session from one command.
- [awrun](https://aitherium.github.io/awrun/) — A priority-aware queue and dispatcher for agentic runs and ad-hoc CI builds. It also judges whether the runner pool is big enough for the queue it is draining, and can ask a host to grow it -- reserving capacity is zero-sum, so a saturated pool needs more of it, not a different share of it.
